b3985c4c90.why: The arbitrary clamp and shuffle controls require both vector pipelines, and the stores, pointer updates, and final comparison are all needed.

6010e9456b.why: All three vector destinations and the cleared r12 are live, requiring four instructions even though two constants are identical.

ea421ad00a.why: SSE2 needs the word load with sign extension, transfer, and broadcast, plus the independent pointer load.

576b48a7bf.why: SHUFPS gathers the low dwords of both pairs of products, and PSHUFD restores their order, replacing two shuffles and an unpack with two instructions.

64e8d516d7.why: Reuse the unchanged shuffled multiplier in xmm8 for both products. Each product also uses SHUFPS and PSHUFD to replace the original three-instruction assembly of its low dwords.

c595ca8dc3.why: The three live vector copies and the independent clearing of r12 each require an instruction.

84487c36ed.why: All three vector destinations and the cleared r12 are live, so replacing a duplicate constant load with a copy would not reduce the count.

70873510f9.why: The scalar sign extension, vector transfer, broadcast, and pointer load are needed because SSE4.1 packed word sign-extension loads would read beyond the original two-byte load.

93cb69dd2b.why: The widening, multiplication, accumulation, index increment, and comparison each produce required results and cannot be combined within SSE4.1.

08ada9ea6b.why: The widening, two products, two accumulations, index increment, and comparison are all needed for the live results.

4c2292f093.why: Each of the three live vector destinations needs its copy, and r12 needs a separate clearing instruction.

6a6a9b0a65.why: The three full-width vector results and cleared r12 require four instructions despite the duplicate constant.

cb00417786.why: Three independent live ymm copies and the clearing of r12 leave no removable instruction.

01aabc5f50.why: The two scalar broadcasts, vector zero, and pointer/index calculations are necessary, including the 32-bit truncation before the 64-bit negation.

4e2e810691.why: Arbitrary unpack operands, coefficients, and biases require both multiply-add paths, their shifts and saturating pack, followed by the store and flag-producing increment.

ce33a67bcd.why: Both broadcasts, the vector zero, and both pointer updates are live, and the index must retain the original 32-bit shift followed by 64-bit negation.

13c7f852dc.why: Both buffers require independent unpack, multiply-add, bias, shift, and pack operations for arbitrary vector inputs, with both stores and the final index update preserved.

c5a48bd303.why: The dword and qword broadcasts, constant load, and pointer/index calculations each require their existing instructions.

a7ae17eb5d.rewrite:
movdqu xmm0,XMMWORD PTR [rdi+rsi*1]
pshufd xmm1,xmm0,0xb1
pmuldq xmm0,xmm2
pmuldq xmm1,xmm2
paddq xmm0,xmm3
paddq xmm1,xmm3
psrlq xmm0,0x12
psllq xmm1,0xe
pblendw xmm0,xmm1,0xcc
pminsd xmm0,xmm4
movdqu XMMWORD PTR [rdi+rsi*1],xmm0
add rsi,0x10
a7ae17eb5d.why: Shifting the odd qword results left by 14 places their original bits 18 through 49 in the high dwords. PBLENDW then interleaves these with the right-shifted even results, replacing both shuffles and the unpack with one blend.

c1edd62314.why: Both broadcasts, the constant load, both pointer updates, and the truncated shift followed by 64-bit negation are required for the live outputs.
